subject: Preflight: session token velocity & latency budget inventory
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@keplerai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: session token velocity & latency budget inventory

Hi Samira —

Thanks for taking the pre-sales call earlier. To finish our sizing pass and propose a committed footprint we need a short inventory of your traffic and latency expectations. Attached is a tiny CSV template but a short reply with the values below works fine. Could you send this by EOD Wednesday PDT?

Key datapoints we need:
- Average concurrent active sessions (chat sessions that maintain KV cache)
- Peak QPS (requests/sec) during burst windows and typical sustained QPS
- Avg prompt tokens and avg generated/response tokens (per request)
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming (approx)
- Fraction of multi-turn sessions (>=3 turns) and average session length in turns
- Typical burst duration (minutes) and frequency (daily/weekly/monthly)
- P99 tail latency SLO target (ms) for short-running prompts (<=512 tokens)
- Any latency tiering or fallbacks required (e.g., route to smaller model at 500ms)
- KV cache reuse rate (approx % of tokens served from cache vs regenerated)
- Preferred GPU SKUs if you have hardware constraints or cost targets
- Any quantization tolerance or quality guardrails we should know about

If you can attach a sample of anonymized logs (csv) with timestamp, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, and model_type that will let us run a quick token-velocity simulation and recommend a GPU mix.

I attached the CSV template for convenience. Happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through if that helps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@keplerai.com>

Cc: procure@keplerai.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: session token velocity & latency budget inventory

Neha —

Thanks, and apologies for the slow reply. I attached a small export (kepler-traffic-sample.csv) with a week of anonymized traffic. Quick answers below based on that sample and our product analytics team:

- Avg concurrent active sessions: 1,900
- Peak QPS (burst): 3,800 req/s (burst typically 7–10 minutes)
- Sustained QPS (business hours): ~920 req/s
- Avg prompt tokens: 45
- Avg response tokens: 210
- Streaming requests: ~12% (mostly long-form generation)
- Multi-turn sessions (>=3 turns): 38%; avg session length: 4.4 turns
- Typical burst cadence: 2–3 times per day (morning, lunch, evening spikes)
- P99 latency SLO target: 600 ms for 512-token workloads (we can tolerate 750ms for peak windows)
- Latency fallbacks: prefer graceful degradation to a smaller model; must not return 5xx unless circuit tripped
- KV cache reuse rate: ~22% (many sessions are short-lived)
- Preferred GPUs: cost-sensitive — open to suggestions (we currently run mixed fleet)
- Quantization tolerance: willing to accept 4-bit/8-bit quantization for non-streaming workloads if quality checks pass

I also copied procurement for the pricing/contract side. Let me know if you need anything else before a sizing recommendation.

Cheers,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
KeplerAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@keplerai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: session token velocity & latency budget inventory

Samira / Neha —

Great dataset, Samira — thanks. A couple of quick notes from a capacity perspective after a fast token-velocity pass:

- Burst shaping: given ~3,800 req/s with 210 response tokens, peak token emission is substantial. We recommend tempering the burst with a short-lived autoscale buffer and a 10–15 minute burst window with a graded routing policy (primary H100-backed tier, secondary A100-80GB, fallback small-opt model).
- Suggested GPU mix (initial recommendation): 50% H100 (GPU-intensive gen), 30% A100-80GB (steady gen & caching), 20% T4s or A10s for embeddings/cheap rerank workloads. This is a starting point — we can make it more cost-informed once we run the traffic simulator across quantized variants.
- Latency: you noted 600ms p99 SLO. For the given token mix we can meet ~600ms on H100-backed instances with continuous batching up to 512 tokens; hitting it on A100 at high occupancy may require conservative concurrency per device. We'll include conservative occupancy curves in the sizing doc.
- KV cache: 22% reuse suggests limited efficiency from prefix cache; we will still size an LRU-friendly cache tier but cannot rely on cache-amortized token cost heavily.

Neha/Karthik — can we book a 20-min alignment call today or tomorrow with Samira and Kepler procurement to walk the proposed commitment sizing and the fallback policy? I can present the initial GPU mix and a cost delta table (A vs H vs quantized).

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Pre-sales Solutions
Redwood Inference
